target_customer: Drayage trucking companies, shippers and logistics companies that pay demurrage, detention and per diem fees at US ports
problem: Containers sit in port terminals and generate late fees that are hard to track, forecast or dispute across many terminals and carriers.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for container tracking, fee monitoring and dispute documentation

founders.name: Alexandra Griffon
founders.background_notes: Per the YC company page. PR Newswire says the founders worked for terminal operators and terminal operating systems before founding.

founders.name: Laura Theveniau
education: UC Berkeley (data science, AI and entrepreneurship, per PR Newswire)
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; role per PR Newswire release.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed integrations with many terminal systems and appointment platforms plus data aggregation and forecasting; standard engineering with hard data access problems.

defensibility.rationale: Aggregating terminal data is replicable; integrations and customer workflows give some lock-in but incumbents such as logistics suites could add similar tracking (CargoWise later partnered with the company).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found as of 2026; the company stayed independent and partnered with CargoWise and Trinium.

market_need_then: In 2018 Oakland terminals were making truck appointments mandatory, showing congestion pain; the founders came from terminal operations. Specific spend figures at founding not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses bluecargo.io, not the .com; a separate unrelated BlueCargo AS and BlueBox cargo products exist in search results.

identity.voice_and_tone: Company blog posts a lighthearted supply chain news digest titled fresh news brewed by BlueCargo

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself; mostly funding and partnership coverage, plus a 2024 SupplyTech Breakthrough award reported on a listing.

pivots.from: Optimizing container storage and stacking inside port terminals, selling to terminals
pivots.to: Software for truckers and shippers covering dispatch, appointments and later demurrage and detention fee tracking
pivots.why: TechCrunch reports the company says it does not sell to ports but connects to all of them; dates given as 2019 to 2020.

outcome_analysis: BlueCargo started inside terminals, then moved to serve truckers and shippers and found demand in tracking and disputing demurrage and detention fees. It raised a seed of about $4M and an $11M Series A in February 2023 and is still operating, with a modest headcount and no exit, so the outcome is a slow but surviving independent company.
notes: Seed of about 4M is stated on the YC page long description and implied by the 15M total in PR Newswire; no dated source for the seed round, so it is not recorded as a round. No dated competitor found near the 2018 batch; the company site names none. Aggregator profiles conflict on HQ and totals.
